Samir — great to sync. Short recap and recommended next steps below (per our call + the numbers you shared).

Recap of your profile (please correct if I misstate):
- Traffic: 180 TPS baseline, 750 TPS short burst window
- Token mix: ~75% short (50–150 tokens), ~25% long (200–2048 tokens)
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms (short), up to ~600ms (long)
- Data: PHI / regulated 

High-level deployment guidance:
- Hosted API: fastest to stand up; likely won’t meet your compliance requirements for PHI unless paired with our private control plane add-on and strict ingestion policies. Good for initial sandboxing.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended for your profile. Gives isolated GPU pools, predictable latency, and the ability to pin quantized/model variants. Can be run in our VPC or connected to your VPC (Private Dedicated).
- Private VPC/on-prem: best for strict regulatory controls and audit requirements (SOC2 + additional attestations). Operational overhead is higher and onboarding is longer.

Dedicated sizing suggestion (initial estimate):
- GPU mix: 2 x H100-80GB (inference-optimized) + 6 x A100-80GB as worker pool. H100s handle highest-concurrency, lowest-latency endpoints; A100s provide cost-effective steady throughput.
- Concurrency & TPS mapping (back-of-envelope): with Redwood batching and KV cache:
  - Short requests (50–150 tokens): ~250 concurrent streams per H100 at 95% latency SLO => ~2,000–3,000 TPS combined across pool with batching.
  - Long requests (avg 1,000 tokens): concurrency lower (~30–50 per A100), typical throughput ~40–80 TPS per A100 depending on model size.
- Token mix considerations: prefix caching for repetitive prompts will reduce effective work on long requests; if you have heavy reuse we can reduce active GPU count.

Cost & next steps:
- I’m attaching a starter estimate (redwood-dedicated-estimate.xlsx) + a capacity worksheet (capacity-worksheet.csv). Please fill the worksheet with 95th/peak profiles and any model choices (desired model family + max sequence length).
- Proposed next step: 60-min sizing workshop with Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (account lead) to validate assumptions and finalize dedicated SKU. Proposed slots: Wed 7/28 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 7/29 13:00–14:00 PT.

I’ll also flag procurement for an initial contract sketch once we agree on the GPU mix and target SLOs.

Best,

Samir — quick technical note to supplement Irene’s recs. Two clarifying questions + a small optimization tip.

Questions:
1) Long-request distribution: when you say ~25% long requests, is that 25% of calls by count, or 25% of tokens consumed? The sizing changes a lot depending on which is true.
2) Do you plan to pin a single model (e.g., 30–70B class) or expect to route mixed models (small base for short prompts and a larger model for long/complex generation)?

Ops tip:
- If short prompts are highly templated we recommend generating & storing template responses in an internal cache tier (or using prefix KV caching). This reduces per-token compute by ~30–50% in our benchmarks and can let you target fewer A100s.

What I’d bring to the sizing workshop:
- Baseline throughput tests we run (synthetic traffic with your token distribution)
- Expected p95/p99 latencies per GPU class for target models

If you can reply with the two quick answers above, I’ll prepare a tuned runbook and an optioned GPU mix (cheapest path vs performance path).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
